parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead:
Alternating current (a.c.) is converted into direct current (d.c.) using a full-wave rectification circuit. Part of the diagram of this circuit is shown in Fig. 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: Complete the circuit in Fig. 7.1 by adding the necessary components in the gaps.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 7.1 mark with a + the positive output terminal of the rectifier.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The output voltage *V* of an a.c. power supply varies sinusoidally with time *t* as shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Determine the equation for *V* in terms of *t*, where *V* is in volts and *t* is in seconds.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: The supply is connected to a 12 Ω resistor. Calculate the mean power dissipated in the resistor.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A partially drawn full-wave rectifier circuit with a.c. input and d.c. output terminals.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A sinusoidal voltage-time graph with four cycles, voltage axes from −4 to 4 V and time from 0 to 10 s.
